A fake-identity attacker cannot target the same cheap clones every round, because winning reputation requires impressing a fresh, unknowable jury each time; pre-bribing or scripting a fixed jury never pays since the jurors change before influence compounds. Building N identities multiplies cost linearly (per-identity stake, unique history, distinct work quality) while expected reward stays near one honest agent's share, so the marginal clone is pure loss.
